source: ANES 2024 May 19 2026 codebook, printed pp. 82-83 and 102

items.question: How would you rate the Democratic Party?
How would you rate the Republican Party?

instructions: Use a 0 to 100 feeling thermometer. Zero is very cold or unfavorable, 50 is neutral, and 100 is very warm or favorable. Return null for a refusal or unknown answer. This instruction is adapted for synthetic model administration.
primary_population: Profiles whose fixed prior party identification is Democrat or Republican; independents remain in quality and secondary measures but not this primary estimand.
party_variable: V241221; 1 Democrat, 2 Republican, 0/3/5 non-major-party; negative codes missing
units: thermometer points: time-point gap -100..100, before-after change -200..200, difference-in-changes -400..400; range-normalized score = raw / 100, not an SD effect size
primary_contrast: mean[(post-pre)_C2 - (post-pre)_C1] on exactly the same profile x stimulus units
secondary: absolute party gap change for all profiles; no multiplicity-adjusted confirmatory secondary claims
missing: Both items required per time point; invalid/missing/refusal pairs excluded from numeric contrast with counts and reasons retained. No imputation. ANES negative codes excluded; 998/999 invalid.
uncertainty: Seeded crossed profile/stimulus bootstrap, equal profile weights for randomized engineering pool. Intervals describe resampling of mock outputs only.
